classification.difficultyReason: Connect the three overlapping edge sums to isolate a vertex, such as by adding two sums and subtracting the third, then recover and check the other vertices.

content.prompt: The integers on the edges of each triangle below are the sum of two adjacent integers inside the circles. Find the numbers in the circles.

spec.description: Upright triangle with a horizontal base and blank circular response spaces at its three vertices. Left, right and bottom edge sums are outside their corresponding edges. White circle interiors structurally mask the connecting edges; there is no mathematical shading.
spec.mathematics: Top + bottom-left = -1; top + bottom-right = -6; bottom-left + bottom-right = -9.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three edge sums are visible; all vertex circles remain empty.

answer.worked:
Adding the two sloping-edge sums counts the top number twice and each bottom number once. Subtract the bottom-edge sum, then halve.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Twice the top}&=-1+(-6)-(-9)\\\text{Twice the top}&=2\\\text{Top}&=2\div2=1\\\text{Bottom-right}&=-6-1=-7\\\text{Bottom-left}&=-1-1=-2\end{align*}$$
Check all three edges:
$$\begin{align*}1+(-2)&=-1\\1+(-7)&=-6\\-2+(-7)&=-9\end{align*}$$
